prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an outdoor road receding from the bottom foreground into a dark background over 20 metres away, bordered on the left by palm trees and a building roughly 8 to 15 metres behind a foreground cyclist. This helmeted cyclist stands about 1 to 1.5 metres to the left of the camera wearer—within or just at the edge of the camera wearer's arm's reach—straddling a bicycle directly beneath him while holding a phone about 0.3 metres in front of his chest within his own reach. Facing rightward in profile with his head tilted down toward his phone rather than looking at the camera wearer, his lower body and bicycle are largely cropped below the frame in frames 1 and 2 before shifting slightly backward and rightward into fuller view across frames 3 to 5 as the camera wearer turns left. Compared to the sun-glared RGB strip, the depth map clearly separates the bright foreground silhouette of the cyclist, his extended hands, and the bicycle handlebars from the midrange trees and road, and also reveals the front edge of a car entering on the far right of frame 2 at about 3 to 4 metres. However, the map is unreliable where it merges the cyclist's torso, helmet, and phone into a single uniform white depth plane and loses fine spoke and frame geometry around the lower bicycle.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates foreground objects on the left side of the road against an unlabelled black background, placing the helmeted person 1 to 1.5 metres to the left of the camera wearer and directly above his bicycle in frames 3 to 5. Across the five frames, the person remains in right-facing profile looking down at the phone within his arm's reach (and never toward the camera wearer), while his body and bicycle shift from being heavily truncated by the left and bottom frame edges in frames 1 and 2 to showing his torso, hips, and bicycle frame in frames 3 to 5 as the viewpoint pans left. In frames 4 and 5, thebicycle mask splits into two parts—a rear saddle section behind his hips and the front handlebars in front of his thighs—due to occlusion by his body, while both the person and bicycle stay roughly 1 to 1.5 metres from the camera wearer. This map highlights small distant vehicles that are hard to spot against the bright sky glare in the RGB, such as a tiny car mask far down the road on the right in frame 5 (over 30 metres away) and the car edge at the right border of frame 1 (around 3 to 4 metres away). However, the segmentation is unreliable in several places, mislabelling the person's hands, phone, and handlebars as two 'skateboard' instances in frame 2, hallucinating a green 'train' mask behind his back in frame 3, and failing to segment the phone or background trees entirely.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only sparse 2D keypoints for the cyclist standing 1 to 1.5 metres to the left of the camera wearer on the road, omitting the bicycle, trees, and background layout entirely. When visible in frames 1 and 4, the yellow torso and head keypoints orient the cyclist in a rightward-facing profile with his face cluster angled downward toward the magenta hand keypoints held about 0.3 metres in front of his chest, confirming he is looking at his hands rather than toward the camera wearer. The magenta hand skeletons lie directly in front of his torso within his immediate grasp (and roughly 1 to 1.5 metres from the camera wearer), while his lower legs remain unrendered and partly out of view below the bottom edge of the frame. Across the five frames, as the camera turns leftward and brings more of the standing cyclist into view from left to right, the pose detections fluctuate intermittently rather than tracking a smooth trajectory. While frame 4 provides a clear skeletal readout of his right-facing shoulder-to-hip alignment, bent right arm, and overlapping two-hand grasp that is partially obscured by dark shadows in the RGB, the map is highly unreliable overall because it completely misses the body and hands in frame 2, drops the entire body skeleton in frames 3 and 5, and only captures a single arm and head cluster in frame 1.
